findings.text: follow-on: pointer_is_review re-implements a predicate the repository already owns. reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:554 _pointer_role reads the role from the record root and falls back to the node's role with the same strip-and-test, and reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:45 _is_review_run composes it into the repository's definition of a review pointer, also accepting a minted review node id. The addition neither extends nor wraps either owner, so the two definitions can drift -- this one already omits the minted-node-id half, and a later change to what counts as a review must now be made in two places. The layering pressure is real (recovery_watch imports runs, and runs now imports queue_order at runs.py:30, so an import back cycles), and it argues for moving the predicate to a low-level module both can read rather than forking it. Does not hold the node: a freshly dispatched pointer always carries the role, so the behaviour is correct.

follow-on: 'assert refused.value.cap == cap' compares the exception's echoed cap against the same value this test passed in as queue_dispatch(cap=cap), so the two sides move together and the assertion reddens on no regression the node guards, the raise site at reckon/crew/runs.py:617 echoing the parameter it was handed. The sibling at line 96, 'assert refused.value.held == cap', is the half that discriminates: a census that counted reviews would report held=3 against cap=2 and fail there. The echo buys no protection and should not be counted as durability coverage. Does not hold the node.

follow-on: the head arm's gate log, in the run directory of r-20261021T212738927975-a-review-passes-its-sessions-queue-cap, names fd27ce7217bae94d79bf715df649b9fed25e4e40 on its first line, which is the base commit, while the code it measured was the node worktree's uncommitted change: the gate ran at 23:51 and the commit 10f40d447 landed at 23:59. The header revision comes from run-gate.sh:18, 'git -C <node worktree> rev-parse HEAD', which is the worktree head whatever tree the arm ran in, so the line does not name the revision the head arm measured and would not match the promoted commit if a reader compared them. The tree, module and command lines and the passing content disambiguate, and the reviewed manifest's format carries no arm revision for the audit at reckon/crew/reports.py:1269 to compare, so nothing acted on it. Does not hold the node; committing before the gate, or recording the worktree's revision and dirty state, would remove it.
